paragraphs: MOSS-TTS-Nano is an open-source multilingual tiny speech generation model from MOSI.AI and the OpenMOSS team. With only 0.1B parameters, it is designed for realtime speech generation, can run directly on CPU without a GPU, and keeps the deployment stack simple enough for local demos, web serving, and lightweight product integration.

MOSS-TTS-Nano focuses on the part of TTS deployment that matters most in practice: small footprint, low latency, good enough quality for realtime products, and simple local setup. It uses a pure autoregressive Audio Tokenizer + LLM pipeline and keeps the inference workflow friendly for both terminal users and web-demo users.

MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer is the unified discrete audio interface for the entire MOSS-TTS family. It is built on the Cat (Causal Audio Tokenizer with Transformer) architecture, a CNN-free audio tokenizer composed entirely of causal Transformer blocks. It serves as the shared audio backbone for MOSS-TTS, MOSS-TTS-Nano, MOSS-TTSD, MOSS-VoiceGenerator, MOSS-SoundEffect, and MOSS-TTS-Realtime, providing a consistent audio representation across the full product family.
features: MOSS-TTS: the flagship model for high-fidelity zero-shot voice cloning, long-speech generation, fine-grained control over Pinyin, phonemes, and duration, and multilingual/code-switched synthesis.
MOSS-TTS-Local-Transformer: a smaller model in the family based on MossTTSLocal, designed to keep the MOSS-TTS style of speech generation in a lighter model size.
MOSS-TTSD-v1.0: a spoken dialogue generation model for expressive, multi-speaker, and ultra-long dialogue audio.
MOSS-VoiceGenerator: a voice design model that can generate diverse voices and speaking styles directly from text prompts, without reference speech.
MOSS-SoundEffect: a controllable sound generation model for natural ambience, city scenes, animals, human actions, and short music-like audio fragments.

repositories.name: The Correctness Illusion
repositories.description: An interactive AI application on Hugging Face Spaces.

paragraphs: An interactive companion to arXiv:2606.20128.

The industry-standard correctness oracle for a GPU kernel is one line: torch.allclose(mykernel(x), reference(x)) — one shape, one dtype, one seed. Every modern LLM-kernel benchmark uses it. It is blind to whole bug classes that LLM-generated CUDA/Triton code routinely contains.

This Space reproduces three real bug classes from the gpuemu corpus in pure numpy (so it runs on free CPU) and shows the gap directly: pick a kernel, and watch the standard oracle pass a buggy kernel at a benign shape while a gpuemu-style differential fuzz against an fp64 reference catches it.
features: 📄 Paper: arXiv:2606.20128
🗂️ Full GPU corpus + P1–P4 reproducibility harness: dipankarsarkar/gpuemu-corpus
🔧 The checker: Skelf-Research/gpuemu

paragraphs: 传统的工业缺陷瑕疵检测主要依赖于人工目检或使用简单的机器视觉系统，但这些方法存在效率低、准确率低、劳动强度大、易受人为因素影响等问题。单人开发一款基于改进YOLOv8算法的PCB缺陷辅助检测系统，项目提出了一种改进的YOLOv8算法，首先提出一种残差注意力机制，即带有残差连接的CBAM注意力机制ResCBAM，并在YOLOv8模型的头部添加，提高模型提取特征能力的同时防止模型过拟合。并使用GhostConv来替换主干中的普通卷积在保证性能的同时使模型更加轻量化。同时引入WIOU损失函数来代替原有的CIOU损失函数，来避免小目标对损失函数影响过大的问题以及缓解数据集类别不平衡的问题。通过实验结果表明与原始YOLOv8模型相比，所提出的改进YOLOv8模型在公开的NEU-DET数据集上的Precision, F1score, mAP50分别提高了5.6%, 3.1%, 1.5%。(详细可查看代码开源网址)，其中mAP50为79.2%，达到了state-of-the-art(SOTA)水平，显著提升了检测精度与效率，对保障产品质量、降低生产成本具有重要意义。还将模型部署到了WEB端，用户可以访问网页来上传图片或者拍照进行检测，并可以将结果保存。

repositories.name: Vega 0.8B Typed Decisions
repositories.description: Typed decisions with calibrated probabilities, 73k context

paragraphs: One frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B perception stack, read two ways. Every tab shows both, on the same input, so the trade between them is visible rather than asserted.

Measured on the public S1MB evaluator (137 benchmarks, 26,269 decisions) a fitted head lifts Task Avg from 12.75 to 22.56 at +0.063 % latency, and most of that comes from yes/no judgment (boolean 0.131 → 0.333). It is not a free win: where the label space is wide and examples per class are few the head is far worse: −32.5 points on one 268-label benchmark, and it collapses outright on 151-label intent classification, where the engine scores 0.717 and the head 0.000.

So the question is never "which model", it is "does this task have labels". The Space answers that in front of you: change the input until the two readouts disagree, and the disagreement is the answer.

whatItDoes.text: One frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B perception stack, read two ways. Every tab shows both, on the same input, so the trade between them is visible rather than asserted.

paragraphs: This Space generates human:LLM training data for Peacebell, a small language model about World War II trained from scratch. You hold a long, curious conversation about WWII; a strong teacher model answers, grounded in 325 curated Wikipedia articles through a per-turn article-routing (RAG) system. Your questions become the human half of the training data.

Every session is recorded — in full, with your Hugging Face username — to a private dataset for a quality pass: the assistant's answers are edited to raise their quality, and user messages are edited as sparingly as possible. Sessions that make the bar are published under CC BY-SA 4.0 in the ww2-synthetic-corpus dataset for anyone to use. Contributions are anonymous unless you tick "Request credit" in the app (it applies to the whole session); nothing is published automatically.

The teacher is Qwen3.8-2.4T via the Hugging Face Inference Router. Signing in grants this Space the inference-api permission, so the teacher runs on your Hugging Face account and consumes your Inference Providers credits — the Space owner's account is never used for inference.
